brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume using market benchmark and four ready alternates

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm caps at higher volume, down from typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc
priceAsk.basis: Market research shows 28 mm induction-wad PP caps typically ask ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — we want that lower band

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 45 days after receipt

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or cash position. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is small, so we're not a must-keep account for them. That means we push on price and quality using the market benchmark and four strong alternates lined up — Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, the country's largest rigid-plastic converter), Mold-Tek (₹946.50 Cr, listed and profitable), Hitech (₹701.17 Cr, listed) and Pearl (₹19.83 Cr, PET specialist) — rather than trying to squeeze a supplier whose finances we can't see. The 40% return rate is the bigger risk: fix quality first, then use the alternates to justify the target price.

evidence.point: 40% of their deliveries get sent back — quality or paperwork failures are costing us time and money
Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with room down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
evidence.figure: askBand: ₹0.55–1.20/pc; typical: ₹0.85–0.95/pc; verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: HDPE resin import unit value sits at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material floor to benchmark against
Our annual spend with them is only ₹1.66 L — small enough that we can walk if quality and price don't improve
Extending payment by 15 days frees up ₹6817 in cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma; strong and profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) — broad capability across bottles and caps

risks: The 40% return rate is the urgent problem — push for a root-cause fix (process, spec, inspection) before committing more volume, or the savings evaporate in rework and delays
Scorpion's finances aren't public, so we can't tell if they're stretched or stable — keep the tone firm but not harsh, and have Manjushree or Mold-Tek ready to quote if they can't meet our ask
Our ₹1.66 L spend is tiny — they may not bend much for us alone, so bundle the ask: better price plus 45-day terms plus zero returns, and make it clear we're qualifying a second source
Market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads to qualify — verify capability and get quotes before treating any as an approved alternate
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to grow the business with you, but the 40% return rate has to drop to zero and we need your best price — ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume — because we're lining up Manjushree and Mold-Tek as second sources and the market benchmark sits at ₹0.85–0.95 with room to move lower.
